title: TESS eclipse times (2019-2026) confirm the period increase of V617 Sgr, arrive 15 min after the WX Cen decay forecast, and move early in V Sge in 2024 with a light-curve shape change
abstract: V Sge, WX Cen and V617 Sgr are eclipsing V Sge-class binaries, possible Galactic supersoft X-ray sources. Published studies report fast period changes: an accelerating decrease in V Sge (Smak 2022; a merger near 2083 was also predicted), a rapid decay in WX Cen (Zang et al. 2023, -4.4e-7 d/yr) and an increase in V617 Sgr. We measured primary-minimum times in 17 TESS sectors from 2019 to 2026 (SPOC 2-min and our own FFI photometry, four minimum definitions) and did a forward test: we fit each published model to the published minima only, with a season jitter, and predicted the later TESS epochs. V617 Sgr: the quadratic (dP/dt = +1.75e-7 d/yr) predicts 2023-2026 to within 0.004 d (|z| <= 1.15); the period increase continues. WX Cen: the published quadratic predicts the 2023 and 2026 eclipses 0.0105 d too early (z = 2.5 and 2.1; 1.8 to 3.0 over methods); the decay possibly slowed (cubic local rate -1.3 +- 1.3e-7 d/yr at 2026, weak evidence). V Sge: the Smak cubic predicts 2019 and 2022 to 0.001 d, but in 2024 the eclipses come 0.011 d early (z = -3.9). In 2024 the orbital hump asymmetry reversed sign, and in 5-day data pieces the timing residual follows the asymmetry with one common slope (extra 2024 step +0.007 +- 0.006 d). Thus the 2024 shift is probably a light-distribution effect, not an orbital change, but correlated measurement noise explains part of the slope. Limitations: only 2-3 forecast seasons per star; no V Sge data after 2024; pre-1998 V Sge minima not used.

citations.reason: Smak 2022: V Sge minima (Table 1) and the parabola and cubic ephemerides that we test.
Zang et al. 2023: WX Cen minima and the quadratic decay ephemeris; TESS 2023 and 2026 eclipses arrive 0.0105 d later than its forecast.
